newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close lower as results hit SIA.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close lower as results hit SIA.

text.p: Singapore stocks closed lower on Monday, depressed by profit-taking after last week's small run-up and by disappointing first-half results from national carrier Singapore Airlines (SIA).
SIA's foreign share tranche closed down Singapore $1.00 at S$13.00. Its local shares were down five cents at S$7.55.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended 9.35 points lower at 2,067.85, reversing four days of gains between October 22 and 25.
"SIA's results took the market by surprise," said one institutional dealer with a large local bank.
"But some of the blue chips and financial stocks rose today, and there is a general feeling the Singapore market may have bottomed out...Most of the banks' foreign shares rose."
SIA overnight reported a below-consensus 7.2 percent rise in net profit to S$560.5 million for the half-year to September 30.
One of the most active stocks was Malaysia's data processing firm Tongkah Holdings, which rose nine cents to S$2.44 after a European brokerage issued a buy recommendation on it last week.
The biggest gainer was OCBC bank which saw its foreign shares rise 20 cents to S$16.00.
